verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left arm numbness, tingling and some weakness for about 2 weeks: “it's probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks… in the beginning, I just kind of felt a little bit of a tingling… then the numbing kind of started… I will say… it's, like, numb, I can't feel it… you're definitely having some sort some form of weakness.”

She links onset to starting boxing and describes progression from tingling to more severe symptoms: “I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks… it's probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks… in the beginning, I just kind of felt a little bit of a tingling, and then it's gotten, it's gotten worse since then. Then the numbing kind of started.”

Paresthesias in palmar digits 2–4 and fine motor difficulty are described: “it's my second, third, and fourth finger… No. It's… the front side [palm]” and “I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed it's been kind of harder to get the notes.”

She reports transient left-eye visual loss lasting ~20 minutes a few weeks ago: “another weird thing… a few weeks ago, is like, I all of a sudden just couldn't see from… my left eye… that just lasted maybe for, I don't know, twenty, twenty minutes?” and repeats “I think it was only maybe like twenty minutes or so.”
She tried massage and hot baths without relief: “I tried to get a massage, it's not better. Or, you know, try to take warm baths. It's not better.”

Transcript supports viral illness after heavy alcohol use and fatigue, but not headaches as part of that illness: “I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago… we were like out partying until… late hours… And then after that, I was sick for probably good like two weeks.” Headaches are mentioned separately as occasional “tired headaches” related to overwork/workouts: “sometimes I get headaches but I think they're just tired headaches… because I work too much… or… I really just exhaust myself,” not clearly tied to that viral illness.
She denies chronic conditions: “in general, I'm, I'm pretty healthy. You know, I work out… and I, I don't really have any medical problems.”
She uses ibuprofen intermittently: “I do take Ibuprofen because my muscles were sore… I've just kind of taken ibuprofen for that.”

She takes vitamin D and is supposed to take iron but often forgets: “I just take ibuprofen every once in a while, I take vitamin D. Um, I take some I, I like my my GP really wants me to take iron supplements, but… most of the time I just forget.”
She uses melatonin as needed: “And then, sometimes I take Melatonin to help me sleep.”

She reports father’s hypothyroidism and autoimmune issues: “I know that my dad has I don't know if it it's hypo, I think it's hypothyroidism… he's got some autoimmune stuff going on, like that much I know.”
She lists mother’s type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol: “my mom… she's got diabetes type two. She's got hypertension… she's got… high cholesterol.”
She exercises and attends boxing: “I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks” and “in general, I'm, I'm pretty healthy. You know, I work out.”

She describes at least one episode of heavy drinking: “we were like out partying until… late hours, and I just got uncharacteristically drunk for me.” This supports “occasional episodes of heavy drinking” as at least one such episode; frequency beyond that is not specified but not contradicted.

Summary matches her description: left upper extremity numbness/weakness with paresthesia in palmar digits 2–4 and fine motor issues: “I can't quite move my left arm… it's numb, and then I also feel some… tingling in my fingertips… it's my second, third, and fourth finger… the front side… harder to get the notes [on piano]… it's, like, numb, I can't feel it… definitely having some sort some form of weakness.”

The doctor does not list a formal differential including cervical radiculopathy, peripheral neuropathy, median neuropathy, or central process. He instead mentions concern for possible MS: “sometimes you know you do get things like MS, multiple sclerosis.” Other differential diagnoses are not discussed in the transcript.

Matches prior visual history: “another weird thing… a few weeks ago… I all of a sudden just couldn't see… from my left eye… that just lasted maybe for… twenty, twenty minutes?” and again: “I think it was only maybe like twenty minutes or so.”

The doctor voices concern about MS due to neurologic and visual symptoms: “sometimes you know you do get things like MS, multiple sclerosis. So people with multiple sclerosis can have, um, visual problems, like what you've experienced and sometimes you know the odd numbness tingling sensations… it is quite important to find out… that's the most serious kind of thing that needs to be dealt with here.”
An urgent neurology referral is planned: “I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral.”
Doctor only vaguely mentions imaging: “What they… might entail is the brain scan and things like that.” MRI, cervical spine imaging, contrast use, and visual pathway assessment are not specified.

Steroids are mentioned but deferred pending diagnosis: “The treatment for it is actually some steroids… But, saying that, first we need to firm diagnosis.” This indicates treatment is deferred until neurology/diagnosis.

ER precautions were given for neurologic worsening including weakness, legs, headaches, vomiting, fits, visual symptoms: “if there's any weakness… progresses to your legs, or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A and E.” Seizures = fits, ER = A&E.
There is no advice in the transcript about limiting boxing, continuing ibuprofen specifically with food, or avoiding alcohol. These activity/medication/alcohol recommendations are not discussed.

Follow-up plan is limited to urgent neurology referral and A&E precautions; there is no explicit instruction that patient should contact the clinic if symptoms progress before neurology, beyond going to A&E for severe/worsening signs.
